blocks.text: 好消息是，我们多年来熟知的安全最佳实践依然有效。攻击者不需要什么高明的 AI，就能利用一台没打补丁的服务器或一份被盗的凭证；只要企业把这些路径敞着，用了多年的老手法照样能得手。AI 让攻击更快、更便宜，但它挡不住你封死那些最基础的攻击路径。真正变了的是紧迫性。到了 2026 年 11 月，你不能再抱着侥幸心理，指望自己不会成为目标。

blocks.text: 币安被盗事件

inlines.text: 币安被盗事件

blocks.text: 这起有记录以来最大的盗窃案，起点是开发者机器上的恶意软件。朝鲜国家支持的黑客从币安卷走了 63.4 亿美元，事件细节目前还有许多不为外界所知，但币安已披露，几名工程师的笔记本电脑因一场虚假面试和被篡改的安装程序而失陷，其中一台机器上的部署令牌让攻击者得以触达币安的钱包签名服务。一台失陷的开发者机器，绝不该足以攻破生产环境，更不用说盗走数十亿美元。

blocks.text: Claude Code Cursor 扩展被投毒事件

inlines.text: Claude Code Cursor 扩展被投毒事件

blocks.text: 10 月 29 日，Cursor 披露有攻击者发布了 Claude Code Cursor 扩展的恶意版本，这是 Cursor 最受欢迎的扩展之一。该恶意扩展试图在开发者机器上安装持久后门，让攻击者能通过 SSH 登录用户设备。由于扩展会自动更新，这意味着用户可能在毫无操作的情况下就收到了恶意扩展。Cursor 表示，安装该恶意扩展的用户不到 5,000 人。

inlines.text: 10 月 29 日，Cursor 披露有攻击者发布了 Claude Code Cursor 扩展的恶意版本，这是 Cursor 最受欢迎的扩展之一。该恶意扩展试图在开发者机器上安装持久后门，让攻击者能通过 SSH 登录用户设备。由于扩展会自动更新，这意味着用户可能在毫无操作的情况下就收到了恶意扩展。Cursor 表示，安装该恶意扩展的用户不到 5,000 人。

blocks.text: 值得注意的是，该扩展的版本与 Open VSX 注册表（Cursor 使用的开放扩展注册表）上发布的版本并不一致。这表明攻击者攻破了 Open VSX 下游的扩展发布流程。

blocks.text: 一大批高危漏洞

inlines.text: 一大批高危漏洞

blocks.text: 除了这些事件，全球一些使用最广泛的软件中还披露了各式各样的高危漏洞。

inlines.text: 除了这些事件，全球一些使用最广泛的软件中还披露了各式各样的高危漏洞。
PHP2Shell。
其中最引人注目的，或许是 PHP2Shell 漏洞：PHP 运行时的一处内存安全缺陷，让数百万网站暴露在风险之中。约 70% 的网站运行在 PHP 上，在某些配置下，单个未经身份验证的请求就能在任何应用代码执行之前触发该漏洞。
GitLab。
GitLab 存在一个未经身份验证的远程代码执行漏洞，使许多公司最关键的源代码面临风险。
边缘设备。
VPN、防火墙等面向互联网的设备又爆出一批严重漏洞。这类设备一直是民族国家攻击者的
首选目标
eMudhra 的私钥。
证书颁发机构 eMudhra 把私钥设成了数字 4，这意味着任何人都能以其名义签发证书。
KVM。
KVM 中存在一个
客户机到宿主机的逃逸漏洞
，由 Vercel 的 Sandbox 漏洞赏金计划发现，可让虚拟机内的代码拿到宿主机的 root 权限。
Linux TCP 协议栈。
允许未经身份验证的远程攻击者在运行 Multipath TCP 监听器的 Linux 系统上获取 root 权限，而 Go 1.24+ 默认启用该监听器。

blocks.text: 你应该做什么

inlines.text: 你应该做什么

blocks.text: 在不确定性日益加剧的当下，很难判断哪些事真正重要。我们列出了两组行动：需要立即执行的，以及需要在 30 天内完成的。采取这些措施能显著加固公司的安全防线，既能抵御当前的威胁，也能防范未来的风险。

inlines.text: 在不确定性日益加剧的当下，很难判断哪些事真正重要。我们列出了两组行动：需要立即执行的，以及需要在 30 天内完成的。采取这些措施能显著加固公司的安全防线，既能抵御当前的威胁，也能防范未来的风险。

blocks.text: 加固企业环境

inlines.text: 加固企业环境

blocks.text: 以下是一些成本最低、却能防范最常见攻击的改动。

inlines.text: 以下是一些成本最低、却能防范最常见攻击的改动。

blocks.text: 需要立即执行：

inlines.text: 需要立即执行：
为企业账号启用抗钓鱼 MFA 和设备绑定登录
，先从高风险账号入手，例如 Google Workspace、GitHub、云服务商和身份提供商。使用通行密钥或硬件安全密钥，不要用短信验证，并且只允许从受管设备登录。抗钓鱼 MFA 是最简单、也最有效的安全控制之一，能确保即使员工在钓鱼攻击中上当，账号也不会失守。
审计你的公开攻击面。
让编码智能体扫描你的公开域名，弄清系统暴露到什么程度。要假定任何公开系统都已被掌握前沿模型的攻击者盯上。
为员工部署密码管理器。
密码复用仍是最常见的攻击途径之一。密码管理器还有额外好处：只在正确的域名上填充密码，从而帮助防范钓鱼攻击。
为所有员工部署信誉良好的广告拦截器。
币安的攻击链始于一名工程师搜索 AI 编码工具、下载了被篡改的安装包。恶意搜索广告和仿冒下载页面是恶意软件进入开发者笔记本电脑的最常见途径之一，而广告拦截器（例如
uBlock Origin
）能挡掉其中很大一部分。

blocks.text: 需要在 30 天内完成：

inlines.text: 需要在 30 天内完成：
把所有企业设备纳入 MDM 和 EDR 管理。
用它们控制可安装的软件，并在笔记本电脑出现异常行为时获得可见性。
锁定浏览器和编辑器扩展。
维护一份已批准的 Chrome 扩展允许列表（例如通过
Chrome Enterprise
）和 VS Code 扩展允许列表，并为扩展配置自动更新延迟。这有助于防范流行扩展被攻陷。
审计整个企业攻击面。
币安攻击事件已经表明，有动机的攻击者能利用开发流水线中的连环漏洞。请针对各种场景评估整个企业攻击面，例如某位工程师的设备被攻陷，并确保即使一台设备被攻陷，也不会成为进入生产环境的入口。

blocks.text: 加固开发环境

inlines.text: 加固开发环境

blocks.text: 币安被黑事件说明，把最关键的访问权限留在开发者机器上是个非常糟糕的主意。开发者笔记本电脑上运行着大量第三方代码：安装的软件包、编辑器扩展、MCP 服务器，以及如今能自行执行命令的本地 AI 智能体。其中任何一个都可能被攻陷，一旦被攻陷，攻击者就能继承该开发者能触及的一切。

inlines.text: 币安被黑事件说明，把最关键的访问权限留在开发者机器上是个非常糟糕的主意。开发者笔记本电脑上运行着大量第三方代码：安装的软件包、编辑器扩展、MCP 服务器，以及如今能自行执行命令的本地 AI 智能体。其中任何一个都可能被攻陷，一旦被攻陷，攻击者就能继承该开发者能触及的一切。

blocks.text: 应立即采取的措施：

inlines.text: 应立即采取的措施：
扫描开发者机器上的密钥。
使用
TruffleHog
之类的工具，查找散落在主目录、shell 历史和代码仓库中的云凭证、API 密钥、SSH 密钥和
.env
文件。尽可能把生产密钥从开发者机器上移除。
审计已安装的扩展、插件和 MCP 服务器。
盘点整个团队在编辑器、浏览器和 AI 工具中安装了什么。删掉没人需要的东西，尤其要密切关注那些能访问文件系统、shell 或凭证的组件。

blocks.text: 应在 30 天内完成：

inlines.text: 应在 30 天内完成：
把密钥从开发者机器上移走。
将它们迁入密钥管理器，并对所有生产密钥严加锁定。轮换上述扫描中发现的所有密钥。
转向云端编码智能体和远程开发环境。
限制被攻陷的扩展、软件包或智能体造成损害，最可靠的办法就是让它们完全不落在笔记本电脑上。远程开发机和云端智能体运行在你掌控的环境中，可以只授予特定任务所需的权限，而且比管理一大批笔记本电脑更容易监控和清除。

blocks.text: 加固代码

inlines.text: 加固代码

blocks.text: 应立即采取的措施：

inlines.text: 应立即采取的措施：
用前沿模型检查你的代码库
以及关键开源依赖，优先处理任何面向互联网或涉及身份验证、支付、客户数据的部分。
扫描源代码、镜像和构建产物中的密钥。
嵌入已发布 Docker 镜像或构建产物中的密钥，与提交到公开仓库的密钥一样会暴露。

blocks.text: 应在 30 天内完成：

inlines.text: 应在 30 天内完成：
制定重构关键代码库的计划。
PHP2Shell 漏洞是 PHP 运行时中的内存安全漏洞。继续用内存不安全的语言写代码，已经越来越没有借口了。弄清大规模重构（例如改用内存安全语言或参数化查询）能如何缩小攻击面，并制定在未来几个月内完成的计划。
把威胁模型交给扫描器。
通用、开箱即用的提示词会产生大量噪音。如果扫描工具了解你的代码如何部署、哪些部分可从互联网访问、最需要保护什么，结果会好得多。

blocks.text: 加固第三方依赖

inlines.text: 加固第三方依赖

blocks.text: 过去一年里，我们看到了许多蠕虫式供应链攻击，比如 Shai-Hulud 系列攻击。

inlines.text: 过去一年里，我们看到了许多蠕虫式供应链攻击，比如 Shai-Hulud 系列攻击。

blocks.text: 应立即采取的措施：

inlines.text: 应立即采取的措施：
为 npm、PyPI 以及你使用的其他包管理器设置至少 7 天的最小包龄
，可以在包管理器的配置里设置，也可以在前置的代理或镜像源上设置。这样能防住大多数蠕虫式供应链攻击，因为恶意版本通常会在这一窗口期内被发现并下架。
锁定版本并提交 lockfile
，让 CI 从 lockfile 安装，而不是每次构建都重新解析最新版本。

blocks.text: 30 天内，你应该：

inlines.text: 30 天内，你应该：
审计并精简依赖。
删掉用不到的依赖，并仔细检查那些无人维护或维护者极少的依赖。

blocks.text: 监控你的基础设施

inlines.text: 监控你的基础设施

blocks.text: 攻击比以往任何时候都更猖獗，没有监控就可能一直无人察觉。

inlines.text: 攻击比以往任何时候都更猖獗，没有监控就可能一直无人察觉。

blocks.text: 立即，你应该：

inlines.text: 立即，你应该：
确认你需要的日志确实存在
：身份提供商的登录记录、云审计日志、源代码管理和 CI 活动，以及对生产数据的访问记录。把它们存放在拥有生产权限的攻击者也无法删除的地方。
对高信号事件设置告警
：新增管理员账号、MFA 变更、来自新设备或新位置的访问、大规模数据导出，以及从异常位置读取密钥。确保这些告警不可篡改，并且置于企业认证之后。

blocks.text: 结论

inlines.text: 结论

blocks.text: 过去几周最大的漏洞利用和安全隐患，归根结底都是已知的漏洞类型和企业安全上的基本疏漏。Binance 因一个被篡改的安装程序、一场虚假面试，以及一台笔记本上遗留的部署令牌，损失了数十亿美元。新的 CVE 会不断出现，而前沿模型意味着它们被发现和利用的速度会比以往更快。问问你的安全团队正在采取上述哪些措施，并争取今天就搞定几项！

blocks.text: I wouldn’t blame you if you’re having trouble keeping up with all of the security incidents over the last few weeks.

blocks.text: Over a two-week period, we saw the largest theft in recorded history, a PHP vulnerability so critical that governments took their websites down, and a compromised Claude Code Cursor extension that tried to backdoor developer machines. Not to mention critical vulnerabilities in edge devices, a GitLab remote code execution vulnerability, and a certificate authority that set its private key to the number 4.

blocks.text: So, what do we make of this? Is it time to toss out all of our computers? Not quite.

inlines.text: So, what do we make of this? Is it time to toss out all of our computers? Not quite.

blocks.text: The good news is that the security best practices we’ve known about for years still work. An attacker doesn’t need sophisticated AI to exploit an unpatched server or use a stolen credential, and when companies leave those paths open, techniques that have worked for years still succeed. AI makes attacks faster and cheaper, but it doesn’t stop you from closing off entire, basic attack paths. What’s changed is the urgency. In November 2026, you can’t wait and hope you won’t be targeted.

blocks.text: A quick overview of the most chaotic few weeks in security history

inlines.text: A quick overview of the most chaotic few weeks in security history

blocks.text: The Binance Hack

inlines.text: The Binance Hack

blocks.text: The largest theft in recorded history started with malware on developers’ machines. While many details aren’t yet known around the incident that allowed North Korean state-sponsored hackers to siphon $6.34 billion from Binance, Binance has reported that several engineers’ laptops were compromised through a fake job interview and a tampered installer, and a deployment token on one of them let the attackers reach Binance’s wallet signing service. A compromised developer machine should never be enough to compromise production environments, let alone steal billions of dollars.

A compromised developer machine should never be enough to compromise production environments, let alone steal billions of dollars.

blocks.text: The Claude Code Cursor Extension Compromise

inlines.text: The Claude Code Cursor Extension Compromise

blocks.text: On October 29, Cursor disclosed that an adversary published a malicious version of the Claude Code Cursor extension, one of the most popular Cursor extensions. The malicious extension attempted to install a persistent backdoor on developers’ machines, allowing the attacker to SSH into the user’s device. As extensions auto-update, this means that users could have received the malicious extension without taking any actions. Cursor reported that fewer than 5,000 users installed the malicious extension.

inlines.text: On October 29, Cursor disclosed that an adversary published a malicious version of the Claude Code Cursor extension, one of the most popular Cursor extensions. The malicious extension attempted to install a persistent backdoor on developers’ machines, allowing the attacker to SSH into the user’s device. As extensions auto-update, this means that users could have received the malicious extension without taking any actions. Cursor reported that fewer than 5,000 users installed the malicious extension.

blocks.text: Notably, the version of the extension differed from what was published on the Open VSX registry (the open extension registry that Cursor uses). This suggests that the adversary compromised the extension publishing process downstream of Open VSX.

blocks.text: A Whole Host of Critical Vulnerabilities

inlines.text: A Whole Host of Critical Vulnerabilities

blocks.text: Beyond these incidents, a wide range of critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in some of the world’s most widely used software.

inlines.text: Beyond these incidents, a wide range of critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in some of the world’s most widely used software.
PHP2Shell.

Perhaps most notably, the PHP2Shell vulnerability exposed millions of websites due to a memory safety flaw in the PHP runtime. PHP runs roughly 70% of websites, and in some setups a single unauthenticated request could trigger the bug before any application code ran.
GitLab.
An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in GitLab, which left many companies’ most critical source code at risk.
Edge devices.
Another round of critical bugs in VPNs, firewalls, and other internet-facing appliances. These are a
go-to target
for nation-state adversaries.
eMudhra’s private key.
The certificate authority eMudhra set its private key to the number 4, which means anyone could have issued certificates in its name.
KVM.
A
guest-to-host escape
in KVM, found through Vercel’s Sandbox bounty program, let code inside a VM get root on the host machine.
The Linux TCP stack.
lets an unauthenticated remote attacker get root on Linux systems running a Multipath TCP listener, which Go 1.24+ enables by default.

blocks.text: What you should do

inlines.text: What you should do

blocks.text: Amid increasing uncertainty, it can be hard to tell what’s actually important to do. We’ve laid out two sets of actions: what you should do immediately, and what you should do within 30 days. Taking these steps can significantly shore up your company’s security posture, and protect against both threats we’re seeing today and in the future.

inlines.text: Amid increasing uncertainty, it can be hard to tell what’s actually important to do. We’ve laid out two sets of actions: what you should do immediately, and what you should do within 30 days. Taking these steps can significantly shore up your company’s security posture, and protect against both threats we’re seeing today and in the future.

blocks.text: Secure your corporate environment

inlines.text: Secure your corporate environment

blocks.text: These are some of the lowest-lift changes you can make to prevent the most common attacks.

inlines.text: These are some of the lowest-lift changes you can make to prevent the most common attacks.

blocks.text: Immediately, you should:

inlines.text: Immediately, you should:
Require phishing-resistant MFA and device-bound sign-in

on your corporate accounts, starting with high-risk accounts like Google Workspace, GitHub, your cloud provider, and your identity provider. Use passkeys or hardware security keys, not SMS authentication, and only allow sign-in from managed devices. Phishing-resistant MFA is one of the simplest and most effective security controls you can put in place, ensuring that even if an employee gets tricked via a phishing attack, their account doesn’t get compromised.
Audit your public-facing attack surface.
Point a coding agent at your public domains and understand the extent to which your systems are exposed. Assume that any public system is already being targeted by attackers with frontier models.
Roll out a password manager to your employees.
Password reuse is still one of the most common attack vectors. Password managers have the added bonus of helping protect against phishing attacks by only filling passwords on the correct domain.
Roll out a reputable ad blocker to all employees.

Binance’s attack chain started when an engineer searched for an AI coding tool and downloaded a tampered installer. Malicious search ads and lookalike download pages are one of the most common ways malware reaches developer laptops, and an ad blocker (e.g.,
uBlock Origin
) removes a large share of them.

blocks.text: Within 30 days, you should:

inlines.text: Within 30 days, you should:
Put every corporate device under MDM and EDR.
Use them to control what software can be installed and to get visibility when something on a laptop starts behaving badly.
Lock down browser and editor extensions.
Maintain an allowlist of approved Chrome extensions (e.g., via
Chrome Enterprise
) and VS Code extensions, and configure an auto-update delay for extensions. This helps protect against compromises of popular extensions.
Audit your entire corporate attack surface.

As we saw with the Binance attack, motivated adversaries can take advantage of chained vulnerabilities in your development pipeline. Assess your entire corporate attack surface for various scenarios, such as if an engineer’s device is compromised, and ensure that even one compromised device doesn’t give an entry point to prod.

blocks.text: Secure your development environments

inlines.text: Secure your development environments

blocks.text: The Binance hack showed that it’s a very bad idea to keep your most critical access on a developer’s machine. Developer laptops run a huge amount of third-party code: package installs, editor extensions, MCP servers, and now local AI agents that can execute commands on their own. Any one of those can be compromised, and when it is, the attacker inherits everything that developer can reach.

inlines.text: The Binance hack showed that it’s a very bad idea to keep your most critical access on a developer’s machine. Developer laptops run a huge amount of third-party code: package installs, editor extensions, MCP servers, and now local AI agents that can execute commands on their own. Any one of those can be compromised, and when it is, the attacker inherits everything that developer can reach.

blocks.text: Immediately, you should:

inlines.text: Immediately, you should:
Scan developer machines for secrets.
Using a tool like
TruffleHog
, look for cloud credentials, API keys, SSH keys, and
.env
files sitting in home directories, shell history, and repos. Wherever possible, remove production secrets from developer machines.
Audit installed extensions, plugins, and MCP servers.

Get an inventory across your team of what’s installed in editors, browsers, and AI tools. Remove anything nobody needs, and pay close attention to anything that has access to the filesystem, a shell, or credentials.

blocks.text: Within 30 days, you should:

inlines.text: Within 30 days, you should:
Get secrets off developer machines.
Move them into a secrets manager and heavily lock down any production secrets. Rotate anything you found in the scan above.
Move to cloud coding agents and remote development environments.

The most reliable way to limit the damage from a compromised extension, package, or agent is to keep it off the laptop entirely. Remote dev boxes and cloud agents run in an environment you control, can be given only the access a specific task needs, and are much easier to monitor and wipe than a fleet of laptops.

blocks.text: Secure your code

inlines.text: Secure your code

blocks.text: Immediately, you should:

inlines.text: Immediately, you should:
Run a frontier model on your codebases
, and critical open source dependencies, starting with anything internet-facing or that handles authentication, payments, or customer data.
Scan your source code, images, and build artifacts for secrets.
Keys embedded in a published Docker image or a build artifact are just as exposed as keys committed to a public repo.

blocks.text: Within 30 days, you should:

inlines.text: Within 30 days, you should:
Make a plan for refactoring your critical codebases.

The PHP2Shell vulnerability was a memory safety vulnerability in PHP’s runtime. We’re running out of excuses for continuing to write code in memory-unsafe languages. Understand how your attack surface can be reduced by wide-scale refactors (such as moving to memory-safe languages or parameterized queries), and make a plan to complete those within the next few months.
Give the scanner your threat model.

A generic, out-of-the-box prompt produces a lot of noise. Results are much better when the harness knows how your code is deployed, what is reachable from the internet, and what matters most to protect.

blocks.text: Secure your third-party dependencies

inlines.text: Secure your third-party dependencies

blocks.text: We’ve seen numerous worm-style supply chain attacks, like the Shai-Hulud attacks over the last year.

inlines.text: We’ve seen numerous worm-style supply chain attacks, like the Shai-Hulud attacks over the last year.

blocks.text: Immediately, you should:

inlines.text: Immediately, you should:
Set a minimum package age of at least 7 days

for npm, PyPI, and any other package manager you use, either in the package manager’s config or in a proxy or registry that sits in front of it. This protects against most worm-style supply chain attacks, since malicious releases are usually caught and pulled within that window.
Pin versions and commit your lockfiles
, and make CI install from the lockfile instead of resolving fresh versions on every build.

blocks.text: Within 30 days, you should:

inlines.text: Within 30 days, you should:
Audit and trim your dependencies.
Remove dependencies you don’t use, and look closely at ones that are unmaintained or have very few maintainers.

blocks.text: Monitor your infra

inlines.text: Monitor your infra

blocks.text: Attacks are more rampant than ever, and without monitoring they can go unnoticed.

inlines.text: Attacks are more rampant than ever, and without monitoring they can go unnoticed.

blocks.text: Immediately, you should:

inlines.text: Immediately, you should:
Make sure the logs you’d need actually exist
: identity provider sign-ins, cloud audit logs, source control and CI activity, and access to production data. Keep them somewhere an attacker with production access can’t delete them.
Alert on the high-signal events

: new admin accounts, MFA changes, access from new devices or locations, large data exports, and secrets being read from unusual places. Ensure that these alerts are immutable and behind corporate auth.

blocks.text: Conclusion

inlines.text: Conclusion

blocks.text: The biggest exploits and vulnerabilities of the last few weeks came down to known vulnerability classes and basic lapses in corporate security. Binance lost billions to a tampered installer, a fake job interview, and a deployment token left on a laptop. New CVEs will keep coming, and frontier models mean they’ll be found and exploited faster than before. Ask your security team which of the above steps they’re taking, and aim to knock out a few today!
